intro.objective: Compare and order fractions, decimals and percentages by converting them to the same form. Use inequality symbols correctly.
commonMistakes: Comparing fractions without a common denominator — 3/8 looks smaller than 2/5 until you convert them both to decimals (0.375 vs 0.4).
Thinking bigger denominator means bigger fraction — 1/8 is smaller than 1/4.
Forgetting that 0.3 recurring (0.333…) is not the same as 0.3 exactly.
Comparing a percentage to a decimal without converting first — 35% looks bigger than 0.4, but it is not.
methodSteps: Step 1: Convert everything to the SAME form (decimals are usually easiest).
Step 2: Line up the decimal points and compare digit by digit from the left.
Step 3: Use < or > to show the order.
Step 4: Write the original values in the correct order.
Step 5: Check — does the order make sense?

methodReminder: 1  Convert to the same form (decimals best)
2  Line up decimal points, compare left to right

questions.content:
Put these in order from smallest to largest.

   0.3       0.31       0.29       0.305

Use < or > to make each statement correct.

   a) 0.6 ___ 0.58
   b) 1/4 ___ 0.3
   c) 70% ___ 3/4

Convert each to a decimal and order from largest to smallest.

   7/10       0.68       72%       3/4

Here are four pupils' test scores:
   Ali: 17/20     Beth: 82%     Carl: 0.88     Dee: 4/5

Who came first? Put them in order, highest score to lowest.

Write a fraction, a decimal and a percentage that are all between 0.6 and 0.7.
They must all be DIFFERENT values.

A shop has three offers:
   Offer A: 1/3 off
   Offer B: 30% off
   Offer C: 0.35 off the price

   a) Which offer gives the biggest discount?
   b) Which gives the smallest?
   c) How much would you save on a £60 item with Offer A?

Sam says: 'I can always tell which fraction is bigger by looking at the numerators.'

   a) Give an example that shows Sam is wrong.
   b) Explain the correct method for comparing fractions with different denominators.
   c) Put these in order, smallest first: 5/12,  3/7,  2/5. Show all working.

answers.title: Teacher key
rows: Q5: Ali = 0.85; Beth = 0.82; Carl = 0.88; Dee = 0.8 → Carl, Ali, Beth, Dee
Q6: Accept any three distinct values between 0.6 and 0.7, e.g. 13/20 = 0.65; 0.63; 67%

Q8: a) e.g. 3/4 vs 2/3 — 3 > 2 but 3/4 > 2/3 only works here; try 1/2 vs 3/8 — numerator 3 > 1 but 3/8 < 1/2. b) Convert to common denominator or decimals and compare. c) 5/12 = 0.4167; 3/7 = 0.4286; 2/5 = 0.4 → Order: 2/5, 5/12, 3/7
